item.title: MercoPress: The smarter mobile matchday starts with better sports data habits
item.description: Across South America, following sport increasingly means moving between a live broadcast, a score alert, a group chat and a stream of statistics. A supporter in Buenos Aires may compare lineups before a Copa Libertadores match, while a fan in Bogotá follows a club abroad through a phone. The opportunity is obvious: more information, more access and more ways to understand a game. The challenge is knowing which numbers explain the contest and which simply demand attention.

item.title: MercoPress: Xi and Putin reaffirm their alliance on the eve of the first three-way summit with Trump
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin reaffirmed their strategic alliance in Shenzhen on Wednesday, hours before Xi personally greeted Donald Trump at the airport, on the eve of the first three-way meeting between the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States, to be held on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

item.title: MercoPress: Hamburg tribunal confirms it will deliver its Sea Lion order on November 28
item.description: The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea has confirmed it will announce on Saturday, November 28, at noon Hamburg time — 8 a.m. in Montevideo and Buenos Aires — its decision on Argentina’s request for provisional measures to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands. The order will be read at a public sitting by the tribunal’s president, Judge Maurice Kamga.

item.title: MercoPress: Argentina’s lower house debates Falklands sovereignty bill today, with one chapter short of votes
item.description: Argentina’s Chamber of Deputies debates the national sovereignty defence bill from noon on Wednesday, legislation that toughens sanctions for unauthorised resource exploitation in the Falklands. Javier Milei’s government is confident of passing it in general, but does not have the votes secured for the chapter on foreign interference, which requires a special majority.

item.title: MercoPress: Argentina calls Princess Anne’s visit to the Falklands a “provocation”
item.description: The Argentine government on Tuesday rejected the visit by Princess Anne, the sister of King Charles III, to the Falklands and South Georgia, calling it a “provocation” at a time when the United Kingdom, according to Buenos Aires, is advancing hydrocarbon exploitation in waters whose sovereignty Argentina claims. The Princess has been in the archipelago since November 9.

item.title: MercoPress: Microsoft, flights, banks and now the NSA: a week of tech outages in the US
item.description: The highly classified network the US National Security Agency (NSA) uses for its internal communications went down on Tuesday, the latest in a series of technology failures that in less than a week have hit Microsoft’s email, air traffic, online banking and Apple. No sign of a cyberattack has been found in any of the cases.

item.title: MercoPress: Sunday evening planning felt less rushed after a shift at the start
item.description: At 6:15 p.m., the dishwasher is humming and Monday's lunch is still undecided. I used to leave planning until I was already thinking about bed, which made even a short list feel like one more job.

item.title: MercoPress: Venezuela uses US$12 billion in US-supervised oil revenue to prop up the bolívar
item.description: Venezuela has spent most of the more than US$12 billion earned from oil sales under US supervision on propping up the bolívar, with modest results: inflation has slowed but remains the world's highest, and consumption has yet to recover.

item.description: The World’s Fastest Ocean Liner finally hits the ocean floor. The 53,330-Ton S.S. ‘United States’ is now the world’s largest artificial reef. Longer than the “Titanic,” once carried celebrities and politicians across the Atlantic in midcentury style. Now, after decades of uncertainty and rust, it’s taking on a second life as an underwater refuge for marine creatures and curious divers, according to a piece from the Smithsonian Magazine.

item.description: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday denounced in Pucallpa, in the Peruvian Amazon, the “logics of market and exploitation” threatening the rainforest and its peoples, and demanded justice for Indigenous leaders killed for defending their territories, in the most combative speech of his visit to Peru, which ends on Monday.

item.description: The tension between Argentine President Javier Milei and the ruling party’s Senate leader, Patricia Bullrich, has become part of daily life in La Libertad Avanza less than a year before the 2027 presidential election, and over the weekend it reached the international press. item.description: The gentoo penguin (Pygoscelis papua) is one of South Georgia's most distinctive and widely distributed penguin species. Instantly recognizable by the broad white stripe that extends across the top of its head, together with its bright orange-red bill and pale pink feet, it is the world’s third-largest penguin species.

item.description: Princess Anne, sister of King Charles III, officially opened the Falklands’ spectacular new sports complex as part of the agenda for her visit to the South Atlantic islands, which will also include a sea passage to South Georgia.

item.description: US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold on Thursday, November 19, in the Chinese city of Shenzhen the first three-way meeting between the leaders of the three powers, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. item.description: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on Friday night lifted the nationwide ground stop it had ordered in the afternoon, after some four and a half hours of airspace closure that left thousands of flights cancelled. Donald Trump’s administration blamed the failure on overloaded, outdated analogue telecommunications equipment at air traffic control centres, ruled out a cyberattack for now and warned that the return to normal would be slow.

item.description: The British Antarctic Survey (BAS), the UK’s national operator in Antarctica, began its 2026/27 research season in late October, including the largest penguin census ever carried out on the continent, with flights from the British Rothera station and from Chile’s Marsh station on King George Island.

item.description: Leonardo Bertulazzi, a 74-year-old former member of Italy’s Red Brigades, escaped from house arrest in Buenos Aires on Tuesday by abseiling with a rope and harness from a fifth floor, after leaving his electronic ankle tag on a homemade device that simulated a human leg, to avoid imminent extradition to Italy. Argentine police on Friday arrested a Uruguayan man and a Salvadoran woman, identified as suspected accomplices, as they were about to cross into Uruguay.

item.title: MercoPress: US grounds all departing flights over an air traffic control communications failure
item.description: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on Friday ordered a halt to all flights departing from the country’s airports “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety”, following a communications failure affecting air traffic control centres. Thousands of flights were cancelled or delayed and hundreds of thousands of passengers were stranded. The government has so far ruled out an attack.

item.title: MercoPress: Chile tells Argentina “countries do not ask permission” for its ship bound for the Falklands
item.description: Chile’s Foreign Minister Francisco Pérez Mackenna has ruled out asking Argentina for authorisation for the voyage of the Chilean vessel Danstar, which plans to reopen the commercial route between Punta Arenas and the Falklands in December, invoking the right of innocent passage recognised by the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. “Countries do not ask permission,” he said, according to Argentina’s La Nación.

item.title: MercoPress: Leo XIV to 52,000 young people in Lima: “Be passionate about everything worthwhile”
item.description: Pope Leo XIV met some 52,000 young people at Lima’s National Stadium on Thursday, according to El País, in the last event of his stay in the Peruvian capital before travelling to Chiclayo, the diocese he led as bishop. “Someone told me that Peru needs hope. You are the sign of hope,” he told them, to applause.

item.title: MercoPress: British veteran returns to an Argentine veteran the helmet he took in 1982

item.description: President Javier Milei was moved to tears during Pope Leo XIV’s farewell at Ezeiza airport, at the end of a four-day visit, the first by a pontiff to Argentina in 39 years. item.title: MercoPress: Crash Games Explained: Why This Simple Format Became So Popular
item.description: A line climbs across the screen, a number beside it ticks up from 1.00x, and at some unknown moment the line stops, and the round is over. Anyone who cashed out before that moment wins their stake multiplied by the number on screen, and anyone still in loses everything they bet. Few casino games can be explained in two sentences, and that simplicity goes a long way toward explaining how crash became one of the most played formats in online gaming.

item.description: Pope Leo travels to Uruguay just three weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.

item.title: MercoPress: “They all must go”: Peña’s removal fails to calm anger on Paraguay’s streets
item.description: Thousands of Paraguayans celebrated in Asunción on Friday as the Senate removed President Santiago Peña from office, but the joy turned almost immediately to anger among those who wanted a complete change of government. “Out with them all,” hundreds of protesters chanted outside Congress as Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as the new head of state.

item.title: MercoPress: Princess Anne to arrive in the Falklands on the eve of the Hamburg hearing
item.description: Princess Anne, the sister of King Charles III, will visit the Falklands and South Georgia from Monday, November 9, the day before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea holds hearings in Hamburg on Argentina’s case against the Sea Lion oil project, Buckingham Palace has announced.

item.title: MercoPress: What Game Providers Tell You About an Online Casino
item.description: Most players look at the welcome bonus first and the game catalogue second, yet the list of companies that actually build the games often says more about a site than any welcome offer. Game providers are the studios that design slots, develop live dealer tables and run the random number generators behind every round. When you know how to read that list, you learn things the marketing copy will never tell you.

item.title: MercoPress: How Football Grounds Became Part of Gaming Culture
item.description: A floodlight pylon above a row of houses can tell a supporter they are close to the ground before a sign does. Inside, the angle of a roof or the position of the away end can be enough to identify the venue. Football grounds have a visual identity that survives even when the pitch is empty.d

item.title: MercoPress: Leo XIV begins his tour in Uruguay, praising Mercosur and peace and questioning abortion and euthanasia
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Montevideo on Friday, the first stop on his South American tour, and in a speech to Uruguayan authorities praised Mercosur, peaceful coexistence and care for the environment, but also defended life “even that which is still growing in the mother’s womb” and questioned euthanasia, in a country where both are legal and which is considered the most secular in the region.

item.title: MercoPress: Paraguay’s Senate removes Santiago Peña, who is placed under arrest, and Pedro Alliana takes office
item.description: Paraguay’s Senate on Friday removed President Santiago Peña from office in an impeachment trial for “poor performance of his duties” over the collapse of Ueno Bank, and hours later prosecutors ordered him placed under house arrest over alleged economic crimes. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in before Congress that night as the new head of state and will serve out the term until August 15, 2028.

item.title: MercoPress: Peña says he will face his impeachment trial as Argentina denies he has entered the country
item.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña announced on Thursday night that he will appear before the Senate to defend himself in the impeachment trial against him, after Congress failed for lack of a quorum to consider the resignation he had tendered hours earlier, leaving him formally in office. Argentina’s government, meanwhile, denied any record of Peña entering Argentina, following reports that he might have left Paraguay.

item.title: MercoPress: Big Tech loses a trillion dollars in a day after the Democratic win
item.description: Shares in major technology companies plunged on Wall Street on Thursday and in Asian markets on Friday, in a sell-off that wiped hundreds of billions of dollars of market value, on fears that the Democratic victory in the US midterm elections will slow the expansion of data centres and artificial intelligence. The so-called magnificent seven, including Apple, Nvidia and Tesla, together lost a trillion dollars in a single session, according to the BBC.

item.title: MercoPress: Lula sees his win as “a lesson for the world” after setbacks for Netanyahu and Trump
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva described his October 25 re-election as “a lesson for the world” and linked it to the electoral setbacks suffered in recent days by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump. “In the same week, Netanyahu lost in Israel and I think my friend Trump is losing in the United States,” he said on Thursday in a live broadcast on YouTube.

item.title: MercoPress: Watchdog publishes a list of 77 clergy accused of abuse in Peru ahead of the Pope’s visit
item.description: US-based organisation Bishop Accountability on Thursday presented in Lima a list of 77 members of Peru’s Catholic clergy publicly accused of sexually abusing minors, days before Pope Leo XIV, who lived in the country for more than two decades, begins his tour of South America. Victims and the organisation called on the pontiff to take concrete steps, including setting up a truth commission.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Pope begins lengthy trip to Latin America weeks after lung cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo, who had part of a lung removed last month, will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

item.title: MercoPress: Paraguay’s Santiago Peña tenders his resignation, but Congress presses ahead with impeachment
item.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña tendered his resignation on Thursday, cornered by the collapse of Ueno Bank, but minutes later the Chamber of Deputies unanimously voted to impeach him, in an attempt to prevent him from taking up a lifetime Senate seat with immunity from prosecution once he leaves office. The final decision rests with the Senate.

item.title: BBC Latin America: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
item.description: The move follows a bank collapse and after the lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial against him.

item.title: MercoPress: Ibero-American foreign ministers unanimously back Argentina’s Falklands claim
item.description: Ibero-American foreign ministers meeting in Madrid unanimously approved a special communiqué backing Argentina’s sovereignty claim over the Falklands and calling on Argentina and the United Kingdom to resume negotiations, on the eve of the Hamburg hearing on the Sea Lion oil project.
item.category: Politics, Argentina, Falkland Islands, International, Latin America

item.title: MercoPress: One dead and more than 2,000 affected by El Niño flooding in the Galápagos
item.description: Heavy rains linked to the El Niño phenomenon triggered a flash flood on Santa Cruz island in Ecuador’s Galápagos archipelago overnight from Friday to Saturday, leaving one person dead and more than 2,000 affected, according to local mayor Fanny Uribe. Water reached up to three metres deep in some neighbourhoods of Puerto Ayora, the island’s main town.

item.title: MercoPress: Paraguay seeks to return part of the savings frozen at Ueno Bank within 24 hours
item.description: Paraguay’s Senate on Wednesday approved a reform of the deposit guarantee law that would allow customers of Ueno Bank, taken over by the Central Bank on Tuesday, to receive an advance of up to 40 minimum wages, about 121 million guaraníes, within 24 hours of the bank’s resolution. The bill now goes to the Chamber of Deputies, which was due to consider it on Thursday.

item.title: MercoPress: Republicans look for culprits after defeat: Speaker of Congress steps aside and Vance points to Iran
item.description: Speaker of the US House of Representatives Mike Johnson, a Republican, said he will not seek to continue leading his party in the new Congress, while Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the Republican defeat in Tuesday’s midterm elections, an explanation President Donald Trump called “largely true” even as he defended the conflict.

item.title: MercoPress: Peru declares an El Niño emergency in nearly three-quarters of the country ahead of the Pope’s visit
item.description: Peru’s government has declared a two-month state of emergency over the risk of heavy rains linked to the El Niño phenomenon in 1,380 of the country’s 1,891 districts, about 73%, including all the places Pope Leo XIV will visit in northern Peru from November 13. The measure covers districts in all 24 departments and the province of Callao.

item.title: MercoPress: Milei skips the opening of the Ibero-American Summit and meets Abascal in Madrid
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei did not attend the opening of the 30th Ibero-American Summit in Madrid on Wednesday or the dinner hosted by the King and Queen of Spain for the delegations, and that evening met Santiago Abascal, leader of the Vox party, in the middle of the campaign for Spain’s November 29 general election.

item.title: MercoPress: Democrats retake control of the US Congress in a heavy blow to Trump
item.description: The Democratic Party on Tuesday regained control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate in the midterm elections, winning in Republican strongholds such as Texas, Ohio and Kansas in a heavy blow to President Donald Trump, who will govern for the remaining two years of his term with Congress in opposition hands.

item.title: MercoPress: Paraguay takes over Ueno Bank, with 3 million customers, and freezes its deposits
item.description: Paraguay’s Central Bank on Tuesday took over Ueno Bank, one of the country’s largest banks, after its solvency ratio fell below 50% of the legal minimum, and froze all its assets and liabilities, including the savings of some 3 million customers and more than US$800 million in public funds. The bank immediately suspended all its services.

item.title: MercoPress: Trump accepts midterm defeat but says Republicans would have won “in a landslide” had he been on the ballot
item.description: US President Donald Trump said he accepts the results of the midterm elections, in which Democrats regained control of both chambers of Congress, and signalled willingness to negotiate with the opposition, but blamed the Republican defeat on his absence from the ballot and threatened to veto the new Congress’s legislation.

item.title: MercoPress: Markets react to the US midterms: the dollar falls and gold rises
item.description: The US dollar weakened against major currencies on Wednesday morning and gold rose more than 2% to above US$4,000 an ounce as markets assessed the Democratic victory in the midterm elections, which will give the opposition control of both chambers of Congress for the final two years of Donald Trump’s presidency.

item.title: MercoPress: On first Monday in October Falklands celebrates Peat Cutting Day
item.description: Monday 5th October has been a public holiday in the Falkland Islands. This is because the first Monday in October every year has been declared Peat Cutting Day, which is a way of celebrating a long standing tradition and recalling the primary fuel that for decades kept Islanders and their homes warm.

item.description: Paraguay's opposition won the mayoralty of Asunción and held that of Ciudad del Este, the country's two most populous cities, in Sunday's municipal elections, according to preliminary results from the electoral authority. The ruling Colorado Party, however, won the vast majority of districts.

item.description: Indonesia's sports communities no longer depend on one venue or one broadcast. A football supporter can follow club news before breakfast, join a messaging group at lunch, watch the match at night, then debate tactics long after full time. Basketball fans do something similar around IBL clubs, while esports communities add livestreams, creator analysis, team clips, and tournament chats. item.title: MercoPress: São Paulo stocks jump 8% and the real firms after Bolsonaro's first-round win
item.description: Brazilian markets rallied sharply on Monday in response to the first round of the presidential election, in which Senator Flávio Bolsonaro finished ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, contrary to what polls had predicted. The São Paulo Stock Exchange's Bovespa index rose as much as 8% in early trading, above 208,000 points.

item.title: MercoPress: "The end of the PT era is decreed," says Flávio Bolsonaro after winning the first round
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro celebrated his first-round victory in Brazil's presidential election in Brasília with a message focused on change. "Change, the word is change. Brazil can't take any more. The end of the PT era is decreed," he told reporters outside his campaign headquarters.

item.title: MercoPress: Lula bets on education and non-voters to overturn the result in the runoff
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has set education, research and industrial policy as the pillars of his campaign for the October 25 runoff, and urged the more than 30 million Brazilians who abstained on Sunday to vote, after finishing behind Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round.

item.title: MercoPress: US withdraws all its bombers from Britain's RAF Fairford base
item.description: The United States has withdrawn all the bombers it had deployed at RAF Fairford, in western England, a week after the incident near the base that British counter-terrorism police are investigating. Washington gave no reason for the decision.

item.title: MercoPress: Falklands weighs curbs on Argentine visitors after flag-waving incidents
item.description: Amid a sharp rise in international attention on the South Atlantic and its energy resources, Falkland Islands residents have been angered by Argentine visitors seen waving Argentine flags and banners denying British sovereignty, prompting calls from members of the community to restrict such visits.

item.title: MercoPress: Flávio Bolsonaro edges Lula in the first round; both head to an October 25 runoff
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro won around 47% of valid votes in the first round of Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who took about 45%, according to the Superior Electoral Court's count. As neither passed half of the valid votes, the two will face each other in a runoff on October 25.
